newsitem.title: DUBAI: PRESS DIGEST - United Arab Emirates - July 2.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - United Arab Emirates - July 2.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the United Arab Emirates (UAE) press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- An envoy of Saudi King Fahd travelled to Iran on Tuesday on a rare visit, the latest attempt to improve ties between two of the world's biggest oil producers.
- The Gulf Cooperation Council moved a step closer towards a unified tariff system at its recent meeting in Riyadh when it managed to agree on all but 36 commodity classifications.
- Kuwaiti investors are setting up a firm with capital of $130 million to target investment in Gulf utilities and the downstream oil sector, a founder said.
- Gulf investors can now apply for the initial approvals for their business licences by fax, without having to come to Dubai, an official at the Economic Department said.

- About 126.3 million shares were traded on the unofficial Saudi stock exchange in the first half of 1997, and increase of 137 percent from the 53.5 million shares traded in the year-ago period, the Saudi Monetary Agency said.

- Arab Petroleum Investments Corp (APICORP) reported a rise in net income in 1996 as a result of cost controls, increased earnings from lending activities and equity participation. It said net income rose by over 12 percent to $45.1 million.
- The UAE's Minister of Information and Culture said his country's participation in a controversial Arab-Israeli economic forum in Doha in November was linked to progress in the peace process.
- Twenty-two new hotels will open in Dubai by the year 2000, the trade and tourism board said.
